summary: This configuration file sets up a development environment with Docker and Visual Studio Code customizations. It enables automatic code formatting for PHP files using the php-cs-fixer tool, which will run whenever you save a file and follows the PSR12 coding standard. The configuration also specifies where the formatter tool is located and which VSCode extension to use.

explanations.11: The "[php]" key targets settings that apply only to PHP language files in VSCode, so these formatting rules won't affect other file types.
explanations.13: This tells VSCode to automatically run the code formatter whenever you save a PHP file, so you don't have to manually format it.
explanations.15: This names the VSCode extension that VSCode should use to format PHP code—in this case, the junstyle.php-cs-fixer extension.
explanations.19: This setting makes VSCode automatically save files whenever you switch focus away from the editor tab or window.
explanations.22: This points the php-cs-fixer tool to a configuration file that defines custom formatting rules for your project.
explanations.24: This tells the tool where the php-cs-fixer executable (the actual program that does the formatting) is installed on your system.
explanations.26: This enables the php-cs-fixer extension to automatically format your code when you save.
explanations.28: This sets which coding standard the formatter should follow—PSR12 is a widely-used PHP coding standard that defines things like spacing and naming conventions.
explanations.34: This installs the junstyle.php-cs-fixer extension into VSCode so it's available to use for formatting.
